C-PREFS-WRITE-TRUTH.IntentSummary: Make a failed preference write impossible to survive on both layers while keeping the optimistic UX and every predecessor contract byte-identical. Backend (M-005): PrefsState::set (m005_prefs.rs:320-324) and PrefsState::set_many (:332-338) stop being «memory first, disk later, no rollback» — the pre-call values are captured BEFORE the inserts (each key at its first batch occurrence, so a duplicate batch key rolls back to its true pre-call value, never an intermediate batch insert), the atomic temp+sync_all+rename save runs exactly as today, and on a save Err the captured values are restored under the SAME mutex acquisition — a key that was absent before the call is REMOVED from the map on rollback (never re-inserted as Value::Null), the restore touches only the already-held guard (the Mutex is non-reentrant — no re-locking PrefsState call anywhere in the failure path), a loud [Prefs][rollback][BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK] marker naming the key (or the batch size) and the std::io::ErrorKind class records the rollback, the original Err propagates unchanged (the mt_prefs_set/mt_prefs_set_many command bodies keep returning Err before any broadcast), and the batch rollback is all-or-nothing inside the one C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY transaction (one lock, one save, one broadcast — the get_many reader can never observe a rejected intermediate state). The proof seam is the deliberate mirror of set_many_with_rename (:360-371): a #[cfg(test)] set_with_rename(key, value, rename) so pins can fail the final promote of a SINGLE-key write without touching the production path; the failing-first pins prove the scout contract — after a failed set(key1) a successful set(key2) does NOT carry key1 to disk and a fresh PrefsState::from_path re-read has no key1 (the restart leg), a failed batch leaves no batch value in memory and none on re-read, and a duplicate-key batch rolls back to the pre-call value. Renderer (M-011): SET_SINGLE_PREFERENCE keeps the instant optimistic apply and every happy-path byte, but on a rejected mt_prefs_set it restores this[type] to the pre-write value, reverts the language side effect (setLanguage back to the previous language), drops the boot-dirty mark (the change never became truth), logs a loud [PREFERENCES][BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK] marker (the raw error stays console-only in the existing BLOCK_INVOKE_FAILED line) and surfaces exactly one localized error notice from the new preferences.writeFailure.* keys (severity error, source 'settings', no raw error text, no saved-claim); no retry, no write loop — the rollback is a direct state restore, and the watcher replay it triggers is enumerated and idempotent. Restart truth is pinned at both layers (a fresh from_path re-read and a fresh ASK_FOR_USER_PREFERENCE hydration carry only accepted values).

T-001.Title: Failing-first memory-rollback pins: the #[cfg(test)] set_with_rename seam (the mirror of set_many_with_rename :360-371) plus failed_set_does_not_survive_the_next_successful_set, set_many_failure_rolls_every_batch_key_back_out_of_memory and set_many_duplicate_batch_key_rolls_back_to_the_precall_value — red at runtime on the pre-rollback tree

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first proof precedes T-002's implementation: src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs gains the #[cfg(test)] test seam set_with_rename(key, value, rename) beside set_many_with_rename (:360-371) — the exact single-key mirror: one mutex acquisition, guard.set(key, value), guard.save_with_rename(rename) — together with the three inline #[cfg(test)] pins below, in the existing prefs test module beside the :681/:766 set_many pins. The production set()/set_many() bodies stay untouched in this task. Because the seam ships with the pins, the red is a RUNTIME red (recorded per ReferenceState deviation a): the cargo prefs run fails the three new pins' ASSERTIONS on the pre-rollback tree — failed_set... fails because key1 survives the failed rename in memory (state.get(key1) is Some after the Err and the fresh from_path re-read carries key1 once the next successful set persists the whole map), set_many_failure... fails because every batch value survives in memory and rides the re-read, and the duplicate pin fails because no capture exists so nothing restores "before". The red run must demonstrate the survival, not merely an assertion-name mismatch; all predecessor pins (:681/:766/:815/:882/:926 and the rest of the module) stay green in the same run.

failed_set_does_not_survive_the_next_successful_set — the exact scout/R-1 contract with the restart leg: seed a previous generation through ordinary state.set (a non-batch key such as theme); call set_with_rename(key1, a value, an injected failing rename) and assert the Err reaches the caller with the injected message; assert state.get(key1) is None immediately after the failed call — the memory rollback (review minor 2's absent-key case: key1 was absent before, so it must be REMOVED, never left and never inserted as Value::Null); then a successful ordinary state.set(key2, a value) returns Ok; a fresh PrefsState::from_path re-read of the same path carries key2 and NO key1 («после неудачной set(key1) успешная set(key2) НЕ выносит key1; перечитанный store без key1» — the from_path re-read IS the restart leg, R-3 backend half).

set_many_failure_rolls_every_batch_key_back_out_of_memory — the batch twin with the same temp-dir discipline as the :766 pin: seed a previous generation (a non-batch key plus one key the batch will overwrite); call set_many_with_rename with a batch mixing fresh keys and one overwriting key through the EXISTING seam with an injected failing rename; assert the Err propagates; assert in memory that every fresh batch key is absent (state.get == None) and the overwritten key holds its exact pre-call value; a fresh PrefsState::from_path re-read carries none of the batch's new values; the raw store-file bytes stay at the previous generation (the :766 disk-side discipline retained, asserted unchanged).

set_many_duplicate_batch_key_rolls_back_to_the_precall_value — review minor 3's pin: seed dup = "before"; the failing batch carries dup twice with different values ("mid", then "after"); after the Err, state.get(dup) == Some(Value::String("before")) — the capture happened at the FIRST batch occurrence, so the rollback restores the true pre-call value, never an intermediate insert from the same batch.

The pins keep their exact names through the rest of the change (the TargetAssertions pin them); the red run's evidence (the three failing tests inside an otherwise green cargo prefs run) is recorded before T-002 lands any production rollback code.

T-002.Title: M-005 memory rollback in PrefsState::set/set_many — capture-before-insert, restore on the held guard, BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK, batch all-or-nothing under the one transaction

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: T-001's pins have been demonstrated failing-first on the baseline before any production code of this task lands.

PrefsState::set (:320-324) becomes transactional on the memory side: the pre-call value is captured as Option<Value> via the already-held guard BEFORE the insert; the insert and the atomic save run exactly as today (guard.set then guard.save() — the save machinery, PrefsStore::set (:229-231), save_with_rename (:195-216) and save (:221-223) are untouched, no PrefsStore signature change, no clone-and-swap of the whole map); on a save Err the pre-call value is restored under the SAME mutex acquisition and the original Err propagates. Review minor 2, explicit: a Some(previous) restores via the map insert; a None (the key was ABSENT before the call) REMOVES the key from the map (serde_json Map::remove — available, no preserve_order feature, Cargo.toml:28) — the rollback never inserts Value::Null for an absent-before key. Review minor 4, binding: the rollback body works on the already-held guard directly — module-visible guard.data inserts/removals exactly like replace_from_snapshot's guard.data access (:395) — and makes NO re-locking PrefsState call (no self.get/self.set/self.all/self.save anywhere in the failure path; the Mutex is non-reentrant). A rollback logs [Prefs][rollback][BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK key=<key> err_kind=<ErrorKind>] — the key and the std::io::ErrorKind class only, never a file path (the honesty bar; ReferenceState deviation b).

PrefsState::set_many (:332-338) keeps the C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY one-transaction shape exactly — one mutex acquisition, every insert under that lock, exactly one save — and gains the capture: a Map<String, Option<Value>> filled during the insert loop where each key is captured ONLY at its first batch occurrence (review minor 3 — an occupied-check or entry API so a duplicate batch key's capture is never overwritten by an intermediate insert of the same batch). On a save Err the WHOLE captured map restores atomically under the same guard (all-or-nothing: every fresh key removed, every overwritten key restored to its pre-call value), with the batch marker [Prefs][rollback][BLOCK_PREFS_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK batch=<N> err_kind=<ErrorKind>]; the rollback adds no second lock, no second save and no broadcast — the write still fails with exactly one Err before any broadcast, and the get_many reader (:347-355) can never observe a rejected intermediate state because the rollback completes before the guard drops.

Untouched surfaces, verified by diff: PrefsStore::set/save/save_with_rename, PrefsState::get/get_many/all, from_path, the quarantine-on-load path, the migration marker, the command bodies mt_prefs_get/mt_prefs_set/mt_prefs_set_many/mt_prefs_get_all (:429-517 — they keep returning Err before any broadcast; the exact map_err lines are pinned), main.rs (no new command), and the PrefsStore-level set callers replace_from_snapshot (:387-401) / replace_prefs_from_snapshot — the rollback lands at the PrefsState layer only, per the binding fix direction. Behavior note recorded: ensure_migration_marker's ignored-result set call (:297) now also leaves honest memory on a failed marker write — behavior-neutral, no contract change.

T-001's three pins turn green with their bodies unchanged; the predecessor pins set_many_writes_session_profile_in_one_transaction (:681), set_many_failure_keeps_previous_generation_and_never_promotes_tmp (:766), get_many_returns_requested_keys_without_persisting (:815), corrupt_store_file_is_quarantined_aside_not_overwritten (:882) and save_is_atomic (:926) stay green unchanged — the C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY disk-side contract and the C-SESSION-DURABILITY read-only contract are unweakened.
